model.rawSql:
-- Seconds since the newest automation-tick job resolved. The tick is
-- enqueued every minute, so this stays under a minute while it runs.
-- The backward scan of the primary key stops at the newest tick, so the
-- query reads a few rows however large jobs grows. No row (no tick has
-- ever resolved here) is no data, which leaves the rule quiet.
SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - finished_at) AS seconds_since_last_tick
  FROM jobs
 WHERE job_type = 'automation-tick'
   AND status = 'resolved'
 ORDER BY id DESC
 LIMIT 1;

annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}No automation-tick job has resolved for {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }} seconds. The tick is enqueued every minute and enqueues every automation run that has come due, so scheduled runs are not starting. When the tick resumes, reconcile makes up one late run per trigger that missed its time (the "Automation runs made up by reconcile" alert). Read the newest automation-tick rows in jobs: none recent means no worker manager's cron is enqueueing them (worker logs: "automation-tick cron failed to enqueue job"); recent rows that stay unfulfilled mean no worker claims them (the automation lane, priority 5); rejected rows mean the tick fails as it runs (worker logs: "automation-tick").{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about the automation tick. The query reads Postgres through the boxel-db data source: check the database and the data source's connection.{{ end }}

rules.title: Automation runs made up by reconcile

model.expr: sum(count_over_time({service="worker"} |= "automation-reconcile: " |~ "had no live job; enqueued it again|was overdue; made up run|made up [0-9]+ run" [10m]))

annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}Reconcile made up automation runs in the last 10 minutes (make-up lines on the worker: {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }}). It makes up a run in two cases: a run whose queue job was lost is enqueued again ("had no live job; enqueued it again"), and a due time that passed with nothing enqueued gets one late run per trigger ("was overdue; made up run"). Each line names the automation, trigger, slot and run: search the worker logs for "automation-reconcile: ". Overdue make-ups mean the tick was down or late, so check the "Automation tick stopped" alert. Lost jobs mean workers died or gave up mid-run: read the run's job reservations and how they closed.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about automation runs. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}

{{ if $values }}A {{ $labels.service }} process logged "pricing check failed in" in the last 10 minutes (matching lines: {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }}). A process whose startup pricing check fails has no prices: it admits no new automation run (admission refuses with pricing-unavailable), submits no batch, and writes no charge (charged result no-prices) until its PRICING_* variables are fixed and it restarts. The line names every bad variable and what is wrong with it. This alert resolves 10 minutes after the line, and the process stays without prices: confirm each restarted process logged "pricing check passed in". The pricing skill covers the variables.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about the pricing check. The query reads Loki: check the Loki task and its context canceled and context deadline exceeded errors.{{ end }}

rules.title: Automation runs waiting for a worker

model.rawSql:
-- How long the oldest automation run that a worker could claim has
-- waited. A run waits from its job's creation, or from the end of its
-- last attempt when an attempt was lost. A run behind its own
-- automation's running run (the same concurrency group) or a claim hold
-- is waiting for that, not for a worker, and is left out.
SELECT COALESCE(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - min(waiting.since)), 0) AS oldest_wait_seconds
  FROM (
    SELECT GREATEST(
             j.created_at,
             (SELECT max(COALESCE(r.completed_at, r.locked_until))
                FROM job_reservations r WHERE r.job_id = j.id)
           ) AS since
      FROM jobs j
     WHERE j.status = 'unfulfilled'
       AND j.job_type = 'run-command'
       AND j.concurrency_group LIKE 'automation:%'
       AND NOT EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM job_reservations r
              WHERE r.job_id = j.id
                AND r.completed_at IS NULL
                AND r.locked_until > now())
       AND NOT EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM jobs held
               JOIN job_reservations hr ON hr.job_id = held.id
                AND hr.completed_at IS NULL
                AND hr.locked_until > now()
              WHERE held.status = 'unfulfilled'
                AND held.concurrency_group = j.concurrency_group)
       AND NOT EXISTS (
             SELECT 1 FROM job_claim_holds ch
              WHERE ch.concurrency_group = j.concurrency_group
                AND ch.expires_at > now())
  ) waiting;

annotations.summary: {{ if $values }}The oldest automation run a worker could claim has waited {{ printf "%.0f" $values.B.Value }} seconds, and the oldest wait has stayed over 5 minutes for 5 minutes. Runs that wait behind their own automation's running run (its concurrency group) are not counted, so this is the automation lane falling behind: runs are priority 5, claimed by the automation worker pool. Read the Job Queue dashboard for what holds the lane and how many workers serve it; the claimed event's queueWaitMs on the boxel:automation-runs channel gives the wait each run had once claimed.{{ else }}Grafana could not run this rule's query. This is the rule's DatasourceError alert, and its Error annotation gives the reason. It shows nothing about automation runs. The query reads Postgres through the boxel-db data source: check the database and the data source's connection.{{ end }}
